questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been to Australia 2 times previously and knew I had to come back. Going on exchange there, and going while I'm still young, was the obvious thing to do.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information can sometimes be hidden well away on Monash's different websites. In those situations, I E-mailed Monash Abroad who were usually able to provide guidance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance from Monash Abroad in filling out my Proof of Attendance required by UCPH.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not very easy in general, but we were very lucky to find an awesome apartment in South Yarra by reaching out to a landlord renting through platforms such as Airbnb. This is expectedly, however, more expensive than going through more mainstream platforms such as realestate.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive!! So, you should only go for this option if you're renting with other persons or if you're rich, of course.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to figure out what courses were available to register for - both because I was an exchange student where different rules might apply compared to Monash-enrolled students and because Monash up and changed basically the whole selection of courses shortly before the beginning of 2026 around which time the exchange commenced.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mailing Monash Abroad and info on Monash's websites

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful eventually after a loooot of E-mails back and forth with Monash Abroad about which courses I could enroll and why/why not.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make your registration as early as possible - there's a good chance you won't be able to enroll in at least 1 of them and then it'll be good to still have some choices available from the remaining available courses as opposed to if you wait to make your registration in the last minute

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very intensive courses - teaching and exams were done within 1,5 months of the first class lecture. The level was however lower than at UCPH in my experience since there wasn't as many required readings. On a global scale, I would however still say that the level is quite high. The final written exams can be quite demanding when it comes to references, independent academic research and original intellectual thinking since you usually have 7-10 days to complete the exam as a take-home exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Rather similar - class lectures where the professors expected students to engage in discussion. In my experience, there's more of an intensive to participate in class as your participation counts toward your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Overview of international human rights law, International investment law, International mergers and acquisitions, Corporations, ESG and society

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above - especially nos. 3 and 4

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any as I prioritised traveling around the country

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Great Ocean Road, Canberra (really strange city but awesome nature outside of the city), Wilsons Promontory National Park inter alia

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Very hardline neoliberalist capitalist mindset in business and also in the approach to public welfare

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The generally profound love and respect for their nature and the early riser culture, the very positive attitude of Australians

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Choose your courses as soon as possible, 2. participate in class lectures and 3. go for a walk in Flagstaff Garden

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for as many roadtrips in Australia as you possibly can during the exchange. I can highly recommend Great Ocean Road, Wilsons Prom, Daintree Rainforest and TASMANIA!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling with my partner who was accompanying me on the journey

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Running out of time - could have easily done another semester since Australia is such an awesome country

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
